Hi,

I'm looking for recommendations of books or other training materials to learn ggplot2; for a total of no more than $300. I'm new to R and graphics but am an experienced SAS and SQL programmer. -Mary

Hi Mary,

Besides Winston Chang's great new book (I have 2 copies), here are 3 more books in my "using ggplot2 while on a desert island" library:

Michael Crawley, "The R Book, 2nd Edition" ($79.99 at Amazon.com, released Dec 26, 2012) has 2 great chapters on plots. While the plots in Chapter 5 aren't using ggplot2, they give good ideas for plots. Chapter 29 is about changing the look of plots which has a really good section on the ColorBrewer which ggplot2 can make use of. At 1076 pages & 4.8 pounds Crawley's new book is an extensive compendium of many R analysis and graphics. Plus, the 2nd Edition is in color so it's now much easier to read as the examples have the R code in red and the output in blue.

Robert Muenchen, "R for SAS and SPSS Users", ($74.95 at Amazon) is a good book for SAS users using R. Chapter 20 is Graphics Overview and Chapter 22 is Graphics with ggplot2. This chapter was written by Hadley Wickham the creator of ggplot2. I think it is a clearer explanation on the basics of using ggplot2 than what is in his own ggplot2 book.

Hadley Wickham, "ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis (Use R!)", ($56.92 at Amazon) is the foundation book for using ggplot2 and should be in your ggplot2 library. I used this book to teach myself ggplot2, but think it's a better book for using ggplot2 after you know and have used ggplot2 awhile rather than for trying to learn ggplot2.

--Mary
